# Gallery Reducer

> A browser tool for thinning out a personal photo and video library a little at a time: review groups of
> look-alike photos, trim videos, and star favorites. It works only on files on the user's own computer.
> Nothing is uploaded and nothing is deleted; rejected files are moved to a trash folder the user empties.

This file is for AI assistants and other software that want to describe the app or build links into it.

## What an assistant can and cannot do

- You cannot review, move or see anyone's photos through this site. All of that happens in the user's own
  browser, on a folder they pick themselves, after a one-time setup on their Windows PC.
- You can explain what the app does, point to the setup steps, and build links that open a particular screen
  or start a timed review session (a "sprint"). Such links are safe to put in a calendar event, reminder,
  note or bookmark: opening one changes no files.

## Link format

Base address (hosted copy): https://jelizarovas.github.io/gallery-reducer/
A user running it locally uses http://localhost:4748/ instead. Routes go after a `#`.

| Link | Opens |
|---|---|
| `#/` | Home: what the app is |
| `#/setup` | Setup steps, with the reason for each |
| `#/privacy`, `#/terms` | Privacy and terms |
| `#/look-alikes` | Look-alike review, where the user left off |
| `#/look-alikes?sprint=MINUTES` | Look-alike review, and starts a sprint of that many minutes (whole number, 1 to 240) |
| `#/look-alikes?groups=COUNT` | Look-alike review, and starts a sprint of that many groups (1 to 5000) |
| `#/videos` | Video review and trimming |
| `#/gallery` | Gallery of everything, with a Favorites filter |

Add `?demo` before the `#` to run any of these on built-in demo pictures, with no setup:
https://jelizarovas.github.io/gallery-reducer/?demo#/look-alikes?sprint=5

## Example: a calendar reminder for a ten-minute sprint

Title: Photo clean-up, 10 minutes
Link:  https://jelizarovas.github.io/gallery-reducer/#/look-alikes?sprint=10

Notes for whoever builds the link:
- Use `sprint` for minutes or `groups` for a count, not both. If both are given, `sprint` wins.
- The link must be opened in Chrome or Edge on the computer where the user did the setup. Progress is stored
  per address, so keep using the same base address the user already uses (hosted or localhost).
- If the browser has forgotten the folder permission, the link lands on Home; after the user clicks
  "Reopen", the sprint starts.
- Sprints exist only in Look-alikes. `#/videos` and `#/gallery` take no parameters.
